key_insight: For predicting welding outputs, stacking ensemble learning achieved higher task-specific accuracy than multitask neural networks, while MTNN still captured shared patterns across related targets well.
engineering_relevance: The results help engineers choose between a generalizable multi-output model and a more precise task-specific predictor when estimating UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
method: Compared multitask neural network (shared hidden layers + task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding performance metrics: UTS, weld bead hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated performance using RMSE and R² across the shared dataset.
evidence_signal: MTNN reported RMSE/R² of 0.1288/0.6724 for UTS, 0.0886/0.9215 for weld hardness, and 0.1125/0.8407 for HAZ hardness, while stacking improved to 0.0263/0.9863, 0.0467/0.9782, and 0.1109/0.8453, respectively.
watch_item: The better-performing stacking model may be more task-specific and potentially less suitable than MTNN when data are sparse or when shared-task generalization is the priority.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
